sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the paradox of "Mah" (what) becoming "Me'ah" (one hundred) through the addition of the letter Alef, and contrasts the love of "Bechol Me'odecha" in the first paragraph of Shema with the self-sacrifice (mesirut nefesh) recalled in the second paragraph.

translations.translation: And it is necessary to understand,
that in the aforementioned study,
in order that "Mah"
(Malchut,
Memaleh)
should become "Me'ah"
(Arich,
Sovev)
it is through the Alef
(Atik)
that is added to it,
but from its own perspective, it does not have the concept of "Me'ah" at all,
not even in a concealed manner,
and from the language of our Sages, of blessed memory: "Do not read it as 'Mah' but as 'Me'ah',"
that "Me'ah" is the *kri* (how it is read) of the *ktiv* (how it is written) of "Mah"
(for *ktiv* and *kri* are concealment and revelation),
it implies
that in "Mah" itself there is the concept of "Me'ah," except that it is in concealment.
Also, it is necessary to understand what is stated in the first portion,
"with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might," and in the second portion it is stated
only "with all your heart and with all your soul,"
for at first glance,
since the second portion speaks of those who need to be warned, "Take heed
for yourselves, lest your heart be enticed, etc.,"
behold, in the second portion the matter of *mesirut nefesh* (self-sacrifice) is more relevant,
and nevertheless,
the concept of "Bechol Me'odecha"
(which seemingly is the matter of *mesirut nefesh*)
is stated specifically in the first portion.
And the explanation of this can be said,
that the concept of "Bechol Me'odecha" as it is in the form of love
("And you shall love... with all your might"),
since the matter of love is
(like all the *midot* [emotional attributes])
the feeling that one loves,
except that this love is without limit,
it is the revelation of the essence of the soul as it relates to revelation
(feeling).
For the love that comes from the revealed powers
(including also the love from the *makif* [encompassing light] of *Chayah*)
is limited,
and the love of "Bechol Me'odecha," which is without limit, is from the essence of the soul
(as it relates to revelation).
And the revelation of the essence of the soul that is above relation to revelation,
is in the matter of *mesirut nefesh*.
For this that every Jew,
even the most lowly,
sacrifices his soul for the sanctification of G-d's Name,
is not from the feeling of love,
for this that he sacrifices his soul is not from his own will,
but because he cannot separate himself, G-d forbid, from His Oneness.
And likewise, regarding the fulfillment of all 613 *mitzvot* through remembering the matter of *mesirut nefesh*,
that after one contemplates
(and feels within himself)
that through any transgression he becomes separated from His Oneness, like idolatry,
this that he does not transgress the sin is because he cannot separate himself, G-d forbid, from His Oneness.
And therefore, "Bechol Me'odecha" is not stated in the second portion of *Kriat Shema*,
for the guarding "lest your heart be enticed, etc." is
(not through the love of "Bechol Me'odecha,"
but rather)
through remembering the matter of *mesirut nefesh*, by virtue of which one cannot transgress the command of G-d.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "And now, Israel, what does G-d ask of you?" as a request to reveal the inherent self-nullification (*bittul* of "Mah") of the soul's essence, both through recalling *mesirut nefesh* and through the hundred blessings that connect *Chayah* with *Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah*.

translations.translation: And this is: "And now, Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you?"
"Mah" is self-nullification, like "And we are what (*Mah*),"
and it is the essential self-nullification that comes from the essence of the soul.
And the explanation of "what does Hashem your G-d ask of you" is that Hashem your G-d asks of you the self-nullification of "Mah."
And although this self-nullification
(that comes from the essence of the soul)
is always in a state of perfection,
behold, the self-nullification of "Mah" that exists in every Jew is in concealment.
And the concealment is not only because of the animal soul that conceals and hides it,
but also from its own perspective it is hidden,
because it is above revelation,
and "Hashem your G-d asks of you" to reveal the "Mah."
And in this request
(that Hashem your G-d asks to reveal the "Mah"),
there are two matters.
To reveal the "Mah" as it is, through remembering the matter of *mesirut nefesh*.
And also to reveal it through one hundred blessings
(as per the homiletic interpretation of our Sages: "Do not read it as 'Mah' but as 'Me'ah'"),
the connection of the aspect of *Chayah* with the aspect of *Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah*,
through which the "Mah" of the aspect of *Yechidah* is revealed
(for in order for there to be a connection of *Makif* and *Pnimi* [encompassing and internal], it is specifically through the essence).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section concludes that "Me'ah" is the *kri* (revelation) of "Mah" (the *ktiv*, concealment), and clarifies that the *Yechidah* level which connects *Chayah* with *Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah* is still lower than the essential self-nullification of "Mah" that is above relation to revelation.

translations.translation: And based on this, it will be understood that "Me'ah" is the *kri* of "Mah,"
for the self-nullification of "Mah" that comes from the essence of the soul is an aspect of concealment that is above revelation
(*ktiv*),
and "Me'ah,"
the connection of *Chayah* with *Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah* that is made through the revelation of the essence of the soul,
is the revelation
(*kri*)
of "Mah."
[And it should be added,
that also the Alef of "Mah,"
the aspect of *Yechidah* through which the connection of *Chayah* with *Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah* is made,
is lower than the aspect of "Mah."
For the aspect of *Yechidah* through which the connection of *Chayah* with *Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah* is made
(the Alef of "Me'ah")
is the essence that relates to the revealed powers,
and the self-nullification of "Mah" is from the essence of the soul that is above relation to revelation].
